reason: The Pharaoh of Egypt, the chief elite figure in this passage, is portrayed unfavorably as an oppressor of the Israelites. The text explicitly identifies the 'oppressors' (נֹגְשָׁיו - his taskmasters) causing the people's suffering, and God directly states that the Pharaoh will not voluntarily release the Israelites ('I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go'), necessitating divine intervention through plagues. However, this assessment is somewhat qualified by the neutral portrayal of Jethro (the priest of Midian), who appears as an elite figure but is not characterized negatively—only mentioned as Moses' father-in-law. The negative portrayal is concentrated on the highest elite authority figure.
